result.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
result.summary: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop. These results suggest that a poor actor can still teach well, because judging an action after the episode ends reveals the consequences that acting must anticipate. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 ALFWorld 与 WebShop 上比较三种决策模型和三种通用 LLM 作为 actor、judge 与 teacher 的表现，发现它们作 actor 时易被更简单的子目标带偏，但作为看完整轨迹的事后评判者能给关键步骤记功，并将 JEV 作为教师用 GRPO 提升 1.5B 策略的成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 「逐动作是否有帮助」的事后评判与过程级奖励可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的贡献分配和停止决策提供线索，但其为纯文本长程 agent 设定，能否迁移到视觉推理步骤的监督尚需核查。
